Every player gets 3 blind cards, 3 face-up cards on top of them, and a hand of %1$d. The rest of the cards form the draw pile.
Before the game starts you may swap hand cards with your face-up cards. Put strong cards (like the 2 and 10) face up: you will need them at the end.
Play a card equal to or higher than the top card of the discard pile. Afterwards draw from the draw pile until your hand is full again (%1$d). The ace is the highest card.
You may play several cards of the same value at once.
If you cannot play, you take the whole discard pile. That is the penalty. You may also always take the pile when you could play. Then it is the next player\'s turn.

When your hand is empty and the draw pile is gone, you play with your face-up cards on the table. Then your blind cards: you turn one over. If it fits, it is played; if not, you take the pile plus that card.

Gambling: you may turn over the top card of the draw pile. If it fits, it is played; otherwise you take the pile.

Play goes on until only one player has cards left: the loser.
The game stops as soon as the first player is out. The others are ranked by the number of cards they have left.
Cards you may play are highlighted. Swipe a card up to the pile to play it; to play several cards of the same value at once, tap them first. Pull the discard pile towards you to take it.

By default the app does not enforce the rules: you can put down any card, just like at a real table. Everyone sees the pile, so watch out! Think someone cheated? Tap \"Cheat!\" within 10 seconds, even if others have played since; with several suspicious plays you pick which one. Caught straight away, the cheater gets the cards back, takes the pile as well and loses the turn; caught later, the cheater takes the pile as it is then. Wrong? Then you take the pile. You cannot go out with a cheated last card. Bots play fair but do catch you. The host (or you, against bots) can tick \"Enforce rules\" when starting.

Without \"Enforce rules\" you can put down any card. Call \"Cheat!\" within 10 seconds, also when others have played since: caught straight away, the cheater gets the cards back plus 2 penalty cards; caught later, the cheater draws the 2 penalty cards. Wrong? Then you draw 2.
